category_title: Dominant preschool children who frequently report peers' norm violations
minimal_context: Jack is participating in free play at the art and block stations with his peers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jack, you and Matthew can use the building blocks to make a tower, or use the scissors and paintbrushes at the art table.

STUDENT: Teacher, I want to paint but she’s not ﬁnished yet [with the paintbrush]; she won’t hurry up.

TUTOR: Just see if you can find something else to do while you wait.

STUDENT: (Walks over to the blocks) Give me those blocks, Matthew. If you don't give them to me, I’m telling the teacher!

TUTOR: Try to play nicely and work it out together.

STUDENT: Teacher! Matthew, he’s knocking down the tower! And he won’t let me have the scissors! You need to punish him!

options.A: Use a visual check-in chart during free play, matching numbers, colors, and faces to feeling words on a 5-point scale.
options.B: Acknowledge the report by agreeing or sympathizing with the student, but do not say anything to Matthew about the reported behavior.
options.C: Have more new materials handy at the stations, such as more motivating art supplies or building blocks.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each free play activity at the art and block stations.
